chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you go out for your needs after the obligatory prayer, pray two Rak'at. When you finish the Tashahhud, say: 'O Allah, I have gone out seeking from Your Grace as You commanded me, so provide me with a permissible, goodly sustenance and grant me well-being in what You have provided me.' Repeat this three times.

Then pray two more Rak'at. When you finish the Tashahhud, say: 'By the might and power of Allah, I go out without any might or power from myself, but by Your might, O Lord, and Your power. I disassociate from might and power [in myself] and turn to You. O Allah, I ask You for the blessings of this day and its people, and I ask You to provide me from Your Grace with a broad, goodly, permissible sustenance, which You bring to me by Your might and power, while I am humble in Your well-being.' Say this three times.

key_terms.بِحَوْلِ اللَّهِ وَ قُوَّتِهِ: By the might and power of Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the specific prayers and supplications to recite when going out to seek lawful livelihood?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith details the specific Sunnah of Salat al-Rizq, prescribing two sets of two Rak'at prayers with distinct supplications to seek lawful sustenance after the obligatory prayer. The first supplication focuses on asking for halal provision as commanded by God, while the second emphasizes reliance on divine power (bi-hawlihi wa quwwatihi) and seeks blessings for the day, reflecting the Shia emphasis on combining ritual worship with active supplication for worldly needs.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdulah Bin Al-Mugheira, from Al-Waleed Bin Sabeeh, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When you go regarding your needs after having performed the Obligatory Salāt, so pray two Rak’at of Salāt, and when you are free from the Tashahhud, say, ‘O Allahazwj! I am going out seeking from Yourazwj Grace just as Youazwj Commanded me to, therefore Sustain me with a Permissible goodly sustenance and Grant me in what would sustain my well-being’ – repeating it three times. Then you should pray two other Rak’at of Salāt.

So when you are free from the Tashahhud, say, ‘By the Might of Allahazwj and Hisazwj Strength I am going, without there being any might from me nor strength, but by Yourazwj Might, O Lordazwj! I ask Youazwj for Blessings of this day and Blessings of its people, and I ask Youazwj if Youazwj could Sustain me from Yourazwj Grace with extensive goodly Permissible sustenance, ushered towards me by Yourazwj Might and Yourazwj Strength, and I am free from anxiety in Yourazwj well-being’ – saying it thrice’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Walid ibn Sabih who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when you in the morning after Salah (prayer) want to go to work, perform two Rak‘at Salah (prayer). After saying the testimonies say, ‘O Lord, I have attended this morning and I seek favor through Your generosity, as You have commanded, in the form of lawful and fine sustenance with which You will grant me good health.’ Say it three times.

Then perform another two Rak‘at Salah (prayer). At the end of testimonies say, ‘By the power and means of Allah, I attend this morning not by my own power and means, but by Your power and means, O Lord, and I disassociate from all powers and means. O Lord, I appeal to You for the blessings of this day and the blessings of the people of this day. I appeal before You to grant me through Your generosity vast, fine and lawful sustenance which You will send to me by Your means and power so I can live affluently in good health.’ Say it three times.”
